title: deployment.deploy builds at the landed sha, replaces atomically and proves health
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0 for the infrastructure it builds from.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy` (both human-only), and the deploy EFFECT - build the image at the landed HEAD sha (tag = sha), ship it (local: docker run; ssh: `docker save | ssh docker load`), replace the running container ATOMICALLY, probe the health URL until 200 with a timeout that REFUSES, record `moe-deploy-receipt/1`, and KEEP the previous receipt for rollback. No UI - child 3.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT HERE AND CONSUMED ELSEWHERE. The monitoring/rollback row (task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff) rolls back to it. That row is a SIBLING feature row, so it cannot depend on this one under the parent rail - which makes it MORE important, not less, that the kept receipt's shape is right the first time: get it wrong and the rollback row builds against a shape that changes under it.

ATOMIC REPLACE IS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS. A deploy that stops the old container before the new one is healthy produces a window where the product is down, and the operator sees an outage they did not cause. Health is probed until 200; DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES rather than leaving a half-deployed environment.

A PRODUCTION DEPLOY CITES THE RELEASE DECISION when one exists on the goal, and otherwise STATES 'no release decision' honestly - it does not silently proceed as though one existed, and it does not refuse. (Gate 3 is task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5's; also a sibling.)

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): no deployment kind exists. The closest working pattern is `repository.publish` - the human names a target on the goal, the effect runs in the wrapper, a receipt records the outcome (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts, repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts for the receipt shape). Follow it rather than inventing a second shape. THE ENVIRONMENT'S VARIABLES come from the environments model (task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612's children) - another sibling; compose with it if it has landed, and record what you did if not.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy` published HUMAN-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test; verify by deleting each entry from each side and confirming every deletion reds. Deploying a product is never an agent's decision.

The deploy effect is tested OFFLINE through injectable docker/ssh ports asserting the ARGV byte-for-byte: the build tag EQUALS the landed sha, the ssh path uses `docker save | ssh docker load`, and the replace is atomic in the argv sense the port expresses. A tag that is not the sha makes every later rollback and dossier claim unverifiable.

ATOMIC REPLACE PROVEN, not asserted in prose: the OLD container still serves until the NEW one answers health. Assert there is no window in which neither serves - this is the difference between a deploy and an outage.

DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES and leaves the environment in a defined state (the old container still running), asserted with code + layer. A half-deployed environment that reports success is worse than a refusal.

`moe-deploy-receipt/1` records {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, DEPLOYED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring the landing-receipt shape, and THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT and readable - assert two successive deploys leave both receipts retrievable, since the rollback row (a sibling that cannot depend on this one) builds directly on that shape.
DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED (with the last stderr line), DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE each assert code + layer; the build failure carries the tool's actual stderr, not a generic message.

A PRODUCTION deploy cites the release decision when one exists on the goal and states 'no release decision' when none does - assert both wordings. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for lack of one.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
taskRails: ATOMIC REPLACE: the old container serves until the new one is healthy. A stop-then-start deploy is an outage the operator did not ask for.
THE IMAGE TAG IS THE LANDED SHA. Every later claim - rollback, dossier, incident - resolves through it.
KEEP THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT, and get its shape right first time: the rollback row is a SIBLING and cannot depend on this row, so it will build against whatever ships.
FOLLOW `repository.publish`'s pattern (human names a target, wrapper effect, receipt). A second deployment shape is a second thing to reason about during an incident.
A PRODUCTION DEPLOY WITHOUT A RELEASE DECISION SAYS SO. It does not invent one and does not refuse.

DEVIATION I AM TAKING, WITH THE MEASUREMENT (step 3's premise):
`GOAL_HANDLERS` is a `HandlerTable` of SYNCHRONOUS `CommandHandler`s returning `ServiceOutcome` (bootstrap-ledger.ts). The engine's `createDeployService(...).deploy` is `async` — it awaits docker build, transfer, start and a health poll. A sync handler cannot express it, so `"deployment.deploy": <thin adapter>` in GOAL_HANDLERS does not typecheck and is not a smaller path.

The seam that DOES express it landed AFTER this plan was written (plan 2026-09-05T18:56Z; `repository.bootstrap` landed 01:21Z today): `CommandRegistryEntry.asyncHandler` (http-contract.ts:204-213), with entries built in `daemon-command-async-entries.ts` and spread into `asyncEntries` at `daemon-command-registry.ts:273`. `entryOf` (:288-295) answers the async entry FIRST and returns it whole, so an async kind needs no registry line either — the same "no edit to the oversized registry" property step 3 was protecting. That module's own comment names the reason verbatim: repository.bootstrap "runs `git`, optionally the `gh` CLI and a filesystem tree write, so a synchronous `CommandHandler` cannot express it. It is registered HERE rather than in `daemon-command-registry.ts` ... the registry is past its size cap, and this module is exactly the seam it spreads for async kinds." docker/ssh is the same class.

SO, SPLITTING THE TWO KINDS BY THEIR ACTUAL SHAPE:
- `deployment.set_target` is a pure durable write -> stays a sync `GOAL_HANDLERS` entry exactly as the plan says.
- `deployment.deploy` -> an `asyncHandler` entry via `createAsyncCommandEntries`, wrapped by `commandAuthority.wrapAsync` like every other async kind.
Both still take the plan's vocabulary, bootstrap-contracts, bootstrap-sequence, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and count-backfill edits unchanged; `daemon-command-async-entries.ts` is added to my owned paths and `daemon-command-registry.ts` stays untouched.

ONE MORE GAP THE PLAN DID NOT NAME: nothing persists a deploy target. `DeployTargetPort = (environment) => DeployTarget | null` is declared at deploy-ports.ts:41 and the engine only READS it; `grep -rln "deploy-target\|DEPLOY_TARGET_BOUND\|deployTargetAggregate"` = 0 hits. `deployment.set_target` has nothing to write to, so a small target ledger beside the engine's own (`deployment/deploy-target-ledger.ts`) is this row's to land — without it `deployment.deploy` can only ever answer DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING and DoD 2/3/5 are untestable.

implementationPlan.description:
VOCABULARY: both kinds, operator-only, and the automatic MCP fence. Edit `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, mirroring `repository.publish` at every site:
1. Kind constants for `deployment.set_target` and `deployment.deploy`.
2. Both added to the `WiredCommandKind` union.
3. Both in the EXISTING goal family table with `CAPABILITIES.GOAL`, exactly as `repository.publish` at :75. Do NOT create a new family table — a new table is dead unless it is also added to `FAMILY_TABLES`, because `familyCapabilityOf` walks only that array, and these kinds are goal-scoped anyway.
4. `PAYLOAD_KEYS` entries beside :334 (`"repository.publish": ["goalId", "remoteUrl"]`), mirroring the payload child task-44760ed1 published. Read that entry and match it — do not invent a second shape.
5. Both in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (:376 area).

STEP 5 IS THE MCP FENCE AND IT NEEDS NO OTHER EDIT. mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:78 derives the exclusion from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`; its comment states that a kind becoming operator-only leaves the MCP roster untouched. Because the fence and the payload entry land in the SAME file and commit, there is no landed HEAD at which either kind is MCP-advertised — which matters because the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential.

SIZE GUARD, and it is tight: the file was 386 lines against a 400 hard cap and two kinds add roughly fourteen. `wc -l` it after editing. If it crosses 400, PACK entries onto shared lines the way the file already does at :79 (`"project.activate": CAPABILITIES.ADMIN, "project.bind_repository": CAPABILITIES.ADMIN,`) — do not add a new module, and do not move a table into daemon-command-families.ts, which imports these tables and would invert the dependency.

REGISTER BOTH HANDLERS IN GOAL_HANDLERS — not in the registry, and not in a new table.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts:194` already composes its table by spreading `...BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS, ...GOAL_HANDLERS, ...PLANNING_HANDLERS`, so a GOAL_HANDLERS entry is served with no registry line. That file is 449 lines and ALREADY past the 400 hard cap at the merge-base: add nothing to it, and disclose the pre-existing breach in the completion record so it is attributed to the merge-base and not to this row.

1. `apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-services.ts` — add two entries to `GOAL_HANDLERS` (:199), beside `"repository.publish": publishRepository` (:203). Each is a THIN ADAPTER: validate the payload, call the engine from task-c0e00f0a55ad43bfa5f6b323779834cd with the host ports, return its result. If you find yourself writing docker or ssh invocation here, it belongs in the engine — stop and report rather than taking the extra path.
2. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` — add both kinds to the list at :42 where `"repository.publish"` sits.
3. `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` — declare prerequisites beside :25 (`"repository.publish": ["approval.decide"]`). Decide deliberately what `deployment.deploy` requires (a target set first? an approval?) and STATE the choice and its reason in the step note — this is the ordering an operator will feel.

DO NOT EDIT `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`. Its :238 assertion needs no change when this is done right; it is the tripwire that reds if step 2 added the payload keys while this step did not register the handlers. If it reds, the wiring is half-done — fix the wiring, never the assertion.

HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Add both kinds to the set at `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195`, beside the existing `"repository.publish"` entry and under a comment in the same voice: deploying a product is the operator's decision; the wrapper performs it as an effect of that decision, never as staffed work. DoD 1 states it directly — deploying a product is never an agent's decision.

This is a plain addition: no count guard and no membership guard reads `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, unlike the MCP exclusion roster. Confirm that rather than assuming it — `git grep -n "HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS" -- apps packages tests tools` returned three source files at plan time (agent-spawn-contract.ts, agent-wrapper.ts, http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts). If any asserts a size, that count moves in step 5 too.

ROSTER COUNT BACKFILL — every one of these is invisible to a grep for either kind literal, which is why they are enumerated here rather than left for discovery. Move each by TWO, using the numbers you re-measured in step 1:

- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts` — :862 `ROWS).toHaveLength(N)`, :863 `deps.registry.size).toBe(N)`, :870 `REGISTRATION_ORDER).toHaveLength(N)`; and :1040 `OPERATOR_ONLY).toHaveLength(M)`. A count bumped without its roster entry, or an entry added without the count, is a half-done job the step-3 weld catches. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` after this step and read the OUTPUT, not the exit code.

BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER TEST (DoD 1). Add an arm to `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts`, following the served-origin roster arm already at :795-812.

Assert SET EQUALITY — not a subset — between the ADVERTISED roster and the SERVED set enumerated from the IMPLEMENTATION SEAM: the composed registry's keys and `wiredMcpToolKinds()`, never from the roster constant. A test that iterates the roster shrinks its own iteration when an entry is deleted and stays green while a served capability vanishes from the advertised surface.

DERIVE, DO NOT FREEZE: no count literal and no transcribed kind list in this arm. Assert relationships between production surfaces so a sibling row bumping a roster cannot red it spuriously.

DoD 1 REQUIRES THE DELETION MATRIX, so run it and record every outcome: for EACH of the two kinds, delete it from the ADVERTISED side and confirm RED; restore. Delete it from the SERVED side (its GOAL_HANDLERS entry) and confirm RED; restore. That is four deletions and four reds — "every deletion reds" is the DoD's wording and a partial matrix does not satisfy it. These are TRACKED files, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof; `git status --porcelain` the paths first.

THE JOURNEY (DoD 3, 4, 5, 7 through the wiring) — a new test, `apps/daemon/src/goals/deployment-journey.test.ts`, exercising the REGISTERED kinds through the dispatch seam against a real store. The engine unit-proves these; this proves they survive the wiring.

(a) `deployment.set_target` then `deployment.deploy` succeeds end to end: the image tag EQUALS the landed sha (assert against the sha value, not a pattern), and `moe-deploy-receipt/1` records environment, sha, imageDigest, url and DEPLOYED.
(b) ATOMIC REPLACE through the injected port's recorded call ORDER: the old container still serves until the new one answers health, with NO point at which neither serves. This is the difference between a deploy and an outage.
(c) `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` REFUSES with CODE AND LAYER, and the environment is left DEFINED — assert the old container is still running by reading the port's final state, not by trusting the return value.
(d) `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`, `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`, `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` each assert code AND layer; the build failure carries the tool's ACTUAL last stderr line.
(e) THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT: two successive deploys leave BOTH receipts retrievable and distinguishable by sha. The rollback row task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff is a sibling that CANNOT depend on this row and will build against this shape — so record the exact retrieval call in the completion record for it to use.
(f) RELEASE DECISION, both wordings: a PRODUCTION deploy CITES the decision when one exists on the goal, and states 'no release decision' when none does. Assert both strings. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for lack of one.
(g) An AGENT-authenticated dispatch of either kind is refused with its specific code and the layer that refused.

OFFLINE ONLY, and teardown in a `finally`: no real docker daemon, no network, no leaked container, temp directory or store handle on any exit path including the throwing one.

GATES (DoD 8). Run each leg standalone and quote its `Test Files N passed` count line — the OUTPUT, never the exit code.

- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (@moe/daemon is apps/daemon — resolve by PACKAGE NAME, not directory).
- `pnpm typecheck`.
- `pnpm test` — named by the DoD. State explicitly that the root include has NO `apps/**`, so this leg is NOT evidence for anything this row owns; the daemon leg is.
- ALSO run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` even though this row adds no mirror: this epic's rail requires it of any row in the kind-publishing chain, and two digest mirrors live where the root lane, typecheck and the daemon leg cannot see them. If the sibling row task-44760ed1 already moved them, say so and quote the leg anyway.

SIZE EVIDENCE: `wc -l` every production file you edited and quote it. daemon-command-vocabulary.ts must be at or under 400.

PRE-EXISTING BREACH TO DISCLOSE, NOT FIX: `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` is 449 lines, past the cap, at the merge-base and untouched by this row. Record the measurement so it is attributed correctly, and file it as a follow-up comment rather than a new row.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. Complete only when that intersection is EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW before `moe.complete_task`.

SECURITY-SHAPED, each answered with a command:
- Is either kind MCP-ADVERTISED at this HEAD? Compute `wiredMcpToolKinds()` and assert both are absent. An advertised operator kind means an agent arrives as the operator, because the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential.
- Are both operator-only AND in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS? Assert all three axes together per kind and report which axis failed, not merely that one did — a kind fenced on two of three is the defect class this matters for.
- Does any refusal detail, log line or receipt carry a credential, an ssh key path, or a registry URL with embedded userinfo? Epic rail 3: a secret never surfaces in plaintext, including on the error path.

CORRECTNESS:
- TWO CONCURRENT DEPLOYS to the same environment: does the second queue, refuse, or race the first into a half-replaced container? Assert which — this is the interleaving that produces the outage the row exists to prevent.
- A deploy whose sha is not the landed HEAD sha — refused, or silently tagged wrong? Every later rollback and dossier claim resolves through that tag.
- `deployment.deploy` BEFORE `deployment.set_target`: does the prerequisite you declared in step 3 actually enforce it, with a code and layer?
- If the engine throws mid-sequence, is a REFUSED receipt still written, and is the previous receipt still retrievable? The rollback row depends on that being true.

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths FIRST. The journey test is NEW (untracked), so `git diff -- <path>` certifies nothing for it — back it up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The vocabulary, goal-services and roster files are TRACKED, so `git diff` is a valid restore proof there.
